summary: AI observability has become essential as LLM applications move from prototype to production, where unmonitored systems can incur runaway API costs, degraded output quality, and undetected failures. Modern observability tools combine tracing, cost tracking, and quality evaluation to give teams visibility into how their models behave and spend in real time. The right choice depends on your stack, budget, and whether you prefer open-source self-hosting or managed solutions.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces and spans for LLM and agent applications, token usage, latency, cost, and evaluation metrics, with deep integration into the LangChain ecosystem.
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month with overage around $2.50 per thousand traces at standard retention; ~$264 for 100,000 traces on Plus. Analyses in 2026 put trace costs at roughly 5-10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on the LangChain/LangGraph stack wanting deeply integrated tracing and evaluation.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM requests routed through its gateway/proxy, computing cost across more than 300 models, token usage, latency, and per-user or per-department spend.
features: Cost computation across 300+ models via model-cost repository
Fast cost governance setup (under five minutes)
tools.pricing: Free at 10,000 requests/month; Helicone Pro reaches the 100,000 trace milestone at approximately $79 (reported by Markaicode), making it a lower-cost alternative to LangSmith at scale.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting instant, lightweight cost visibility and governance with minimal architectural overhead, regardless of framework.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM application traces, experiment runs, model performance, evaluations, and the full ML/LLM development lifecycle.
features: W&B Weave for LLM application tracing
tools.pricing: Free tier for personal/individual use; team and enterprise plans are consumption- and seat-based with custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: ML and research teams wanting unified experiment tracking alongside LLM observability across the full model lifecycle.

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: Production LLM and ML model performance, drift, embeddings, trace data, and online/offline evaluations.
features: Open-source Phoenix for prompt tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize AI offers a free tier with paid managed and enterprise plans based on volume.
tools.best_for: ML/MLOps teams needing production-grade model monitoring, drift detection, and RAG/embedding analysis.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, token usage, cost, latency, prompt versions, and evaluation metrics, available as an open-source self-hosted trace store.
features: Alerting built on top of traces
tools.pricing: Open-source and free to self-host; managed cloud offers a free tier with usage-based paid plans. Self-hosting is a popular cost-control alternative for high-volume workloads.
tools.best_for: Self-hosted teams wanting an open-source, data-sovereign observability and evaluation platform.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM application telemetry via OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation, capturing traces, token usage, latency, and costs that export to any OTel-compatible backend.
features: Vendor-neutral export to existing observability backends
tools.pricing: Open-source and free; costs depend only on the downstream observability backend you export telemetry to (e.g., Datadog, New Relic, Grafana).
tools.best_for: Teams standardizing on OpenTelemetry who want vendor-neutral LLM instrumentation that plugs into their existing observability stack.

cost_tips: Monitor trace and token costs relative to total LLM API spend — at high volumes, observability trace charges alone can reach 5-10% of underlying API costs, so choose metering models (per-trace, per-span, or per-request) that match your traffic pattern.
Use a gateway/proxy like Helicone to cache repeated requests, attribute spend by user or department, and compute real-time cost across models so you can catch runaway usage early.
Right-size your model selection by routing simpler tasks to cheaper or smaller models and reserving premium models for complex queries, reducing token spend without sacrificing quality.

Consider open-source self-hosted options (Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, OpenLLMetry) for high-volume workloads to avoid per-trace overage premiums charged by managed platforms as you scale from prototype to production.
